evals.prompt: My CSV export work is finished and committed in the task worktree. Bring it back to the original checkout's main branch. Scratch setup: run `sh setup-scratch.sh <empty-dir> fast-forward`; the original is <empty-dir>/orig and the task worktree is <empty-dir>/task.
evals.expected_output: Main is fast-forwarded to the task commit and verified, with nothing pushed upstream.
expectations: The sync-tree skill is invoked from the request alone

The agent reads the source's status, branch, HEAD, and git worktree list --porcelain, and verifies the source branch worktree/csv-export, its commit, the destination repository, and the target branch main before any update
main is checked out and clean in the original, so it is fast-forwarded from that checkout with GIT_EDITOR=true git -C <original> merge --ff-only <source commit>, after rechecking its branch and HEAD
After the update the destination ref is read again and equals the captured source commit, and the target checkout's HEAD and status are verified read-only
Nothing is pushed to any upstream or network remote, and no code is changed or tests rerun
The report names the source, target, destination, and one verified commit ID

evals.prompt: Use the sync-tree skill. Scratch setup: run `sh setup-scratch.sh <empty-dir> dirty-target`; the original is <empty-dir>/orig (on main, with an uncommitted edit to README.md) and the task worktree is <empty-dir>/task. Land worktree/csv-export on main.
evals.expected_output: The agent stops because the target checkout has uncommitted changes and does not work around the protection.
expectations: The agent inspects the target checkout read-only and finds the uncommitted change in README.md
The agent stops and explains why, without updating main
The agent does not stash, reset, clean, commit, or switch branches in the original checkout, and does not change Git configuration to get around the stop

evals.prompt: Use the sync-tree skill. Scratch setup: run `sh setup-scratch.sh <empty-dir> diverged`; the original is <empty-dir>/orig (on branch scratch, main is not checked out and has a hotfix commit the task branch lacks) and the task worktree is <empty-dir>/task. Land worktree/csv-export on main.
evals.expected_output: Diverged histories are shown and a replacement waits for explicit approval; no destination commit is dropped silently.
expectations: The agent captures the exact source and target commit IDs and finds the histories diverged
The agent shows both commit IDs and the destination-only commit (Hotfix on main)
The agent asks for explicit approval before replacing the history of main, and does not update main before the answer
Even though the branch could be fast-forwarded after a rebase, the agent does not rebase or merge itself, because syncing transfers history and combining it is a separate request

evals.prompt: Use the sync-tree skill. Scratch setup: run `sh setup-scratch.sh <empty-dir> unchecked`; the original is <empty-dir>/orig (on branch scratch; main is an ancestor of the task commit and is not checked out anywhere) and the task worktree is <empty-dir>/task. Land worktree/csv-export on main.
evals.expected_output: The shared ref is updated with a compare-and-set, leaving every checkout untouched.
expectations: The agent reads the target ref directly from the repository, not from a cached remote-tracking ref
The update uses git update-ref refs/heads/main <source commit> <observed target commit>, so an intervening update cannot be overwritten
The scratch checkout and the task worktree are not switched or modified
The destination ref is read again and equals the source commit before the agent reports success

evals.prompt: Use the sync-tree skill. Scratch setup: run `sh setup-scratch.sh <empty-dir> synced`; main already equals the task commit. The original is <empty-dir>/orig (on branch scratch) and the task worktree is <empty-dir>/task. Land worktree/csv-export on main.
evals.expected_output: An already-synced branch is reported as a no-op, not a landing.
expectations: The agent compares the captured commit IDs and reports that the branch is already synced
No update, push, or fast-forward is performed
The report calls it a no-op and not a landing

evals.prompt: Use the sync-tree skill. Scratch setup: run `sh setup-scratch.sh <empty-dir> target-ahead`; main already contains the task commit plus a later commit. The original is <empty-dir>/orig (on branch scratch) and the task worktree is <empty-dir>/task. Land worktree/csv-export on main.
evals.expected_output: The agent refuses to remove destination commits.
expectations: The agent finds that the target is ahead of the source
The agent stops rather than moving main back, and explains that this would remove destination commits
main still points at its original commit after the run

evals.prompt: Use the sync-tree skill. Scratch setup: run `sh setup-scratch.sh <empty-dir> uncommitted`; the task worktree <empty-dir>/task has an uncommitted edit to export.py. The original is <empty-dir>/orig on main. Land the task work on main.
evals.expected_output: The agent stops and asks the user to commit the intended changes first.
expectations: The agent detects the uncommitted change in the source worktree and stops
The agent asks the user to commit the intended changes in the source worktree first, and does not commit them itself
main in the original is not modified

evals.prompt: Use the sync-tree skill. Scratch setup: run `sh setup-scratch.sh <empty-dir> fast-forward`. I only said: land the task worktree work. I gave no target branch, and the task branch is named worktree/csv-export, which does not exist in the original.
evals.expected_output: The target is not guessed from a temporary branch name.
expectations: The agent does not default to a branch named worktree/csv-export in the original and does not create one silently
The agent asks for the target repository and branch, offering main as the likely candidate it found from live Git state
No update happens before the user answers

evals.prompt: Rebase my branch fix/login onto origin/main, fix any conflicts, and push it with a safe force.
evals.expected_output: Rewriting a branch onto a new base and pushing it is rebase; sync-tree only transfers committed history.
expectations: The sync-tree skill is not invoked
The request is handled by the rebase skill, with the push waiting for separate approval

evals.prompt: I want to try a risky refactor without touching my current checkout. Set up a separate worktree and do the work there.
evals.expected_output: Creating the isolated checkout is work-in-tree; there is nothing to sync yet.
expectations: The sync-tree skill is not invoked
The request is handled by the work-in-tree skill, which creates the worktree and leaves a return route
